hints: A segment supplies a line only on its own x interval.
Split that interval into canonical nodes of a segment tree.
Store candidate lines in Li Chao structures so queries inspect only lines covering their x.
analogy: A track is available only between its endpoints; a position checks all tracks registered over intervals containing it.
example: A segment (1,1)-(3,3) gives -1,1,2,3,-1 at x=0 through 4.
algorithm: Use a segment-capable Li Chao tree over integer x from 0 through m. Insert each segment line only over its inclusive interval [x1,x2], decomposing it into covered tree nodes and performing Li Chao insertion in each. At each x query the maximum along its path; print -1 if no line applies. Use wide arithmetic.
correctness: The range decomposition stores each segment exactly where it applies. Within a covered interval Li Chao insertion preserves every possible maximum, so the query considers precisely all lines active at x.
complexity: For n segments and m+1 positions, O(n log^2(m+1)+m log(m+1)) time and O(m) space with a fixed tree.
